sanskrit: śaṃ mā vāto abhi vātu śaṃ me tapatu sūryaḥ | ahāni śaṃ bhavantu me śaṃ rātrī prati dhīyatāṃ śam uṣā me vy ucchatu ||
english: May the wind blow upon me with blessing; may the sun warm me with blessing. May the days be auspicious for me; may the night be laid out for me in blessing; may the dawn shine forth for me in blessing.

sanskrit: ut tiṣṭhata pitaro ye purāsthan yamaṃ rājānam avasānam arcata | ayaṃ nṛṇāṃ nṛtamaḥ śreṣṭha āgan tasmai lokaṃ kṛṇuta yāvatsabandhu ||
english: Rise up, O Fathers who stood in the east; honor King Yama as the final resting place. This most heroic, most excellent of men has arrived — make a world for him together with all his kin.

sanskrit: yasyedaṃ śastaṃ pratimākṛtaṃ devair dattam asūriyaṃ ca saṃbhṛtam | triḥ sapta kṛtva ṛṣayaḥ paretā mṛtyuṃ praty auhan padayopanena ||
english: That which is here proclaimed and fashioned as an image, given by the gods and charged with the sun's power — the seers, having gone beyond, thrust death back thrice-seven times by the stumbling of their feet.

sanskrit: agaman gāvaḥ sadanam agamad vasatiṃ vayaḥ | āsthāne parvatā asthuḥ sthāman vṛkkāv arīramam ||
english: The cows have returned to their stall; the birds have gone to their dwelling. The mountains stand firm in their station — I have made the two kidneys stand still.

sanskrit: ā gāvo goṣṭham agamann āgnidhānāny agnayaḥ | ā vṛkkau sam avitsātām utsaktabheṣajam asi ||
english: The cows have entered the cowpen; the fires have entered the fire-altars. The two kidneys have come together and united — you are the remedy that loosens the obstruction.

sanskrit: yathā dyāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ c- -āntas tiṣṭhati tejanam | evā rogaṃ cāsrāvaṃ ca muñjas tiṣṭhatiy antarā ||
english: Just as the arrow-shaft stands between heaven and earth, so may the muñja grass stand between the disease and the discharge, holding them apart.

sanskrit: asthād idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanam asthād vāto vanacyavaḥ | asthur vṛkṣā ūrdhvasvapnās tiṣṭhād rogo ayaṃ tava ||
english: This entire world of beings has stood firm; the wind that shakes the forest has stood still. The trees standing with their tops dreaming upward have stood — let this your disease stand still.

sanskrit: śataṃ yad bheṣajāni te sahasraṃ saṃbhṛtāni ca | teṣām asi tvam uttamaṃ śreṣṭham āsrāvabheṣajaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ roganāśanam ||
english: Of the hundred remedies you possess and the thousand that have been gathered, you are the highest, the best — the finest remedy against discharge, the most potent destroyer of disease.

sanskrit: yad adya tvā prayati yajñe asmin hotaś cikitvann avṛṇīmahīha | dhruvam ayo dhruvam utā śamiṣṭha prajānan vidvān upa yāhi somam ||
english: When today we have chosen you at this sacrifice, O Hotṛ, as the one who perceives — come to the Soma knowing it, understanding it; firm is the metal, firm and most soothing.

sanskrit: sam indra no manasā neṣa gobhiḥ saṃ sūribhir harivan saṃ svastyā | saṃ brahmaṇā devakṛtaṃ yad asti ||
english: O Indra, guide us together with mind and with cattle; O bay-horsed one, with generous patrons and with well-being. Unite us with the brahman power, with all that is made by the gods.

sanskrit: saṃ varcasety ekā ||
english: "Joined with radiance" — this is one (verse standing alone).

sanskrit: saṃsrāvabhāgās taviṣā bṛhantaḥ prastareṣṭhā barhiṣadaś ca devāḥ | imaṃ yajñam abhi viśve gṛṇantaḥ svāhā devā amṛtā mādayantām ||
english: Sharers in the common flow, mighty and vast, those gods who sit on the strewn grass and dwell on the barhis — let all the immortal gods, praising this sacrifice, rejoice! Svāhā!

sanskrit: yān āvaha uśato deva devāṃs tān preraya punar agne sve sadhasthe | jakṣivāṃsaḥ papivāṃso madhūny asmai dhatta vasavo vasūni ||
english: O Agni, those eager gods you brought here — send them back again to their own seat. Having eaten, having drunk the sweet things, O Vasus, bestow riches upon this one.

sanskrit: ayaṃ no yajño apy etu devān uttarāṃ vedim apy etu vediḥ | vi muñcāmy ṛtvijo dakṣiṇābhir devā yakṣīṣṭa punar uttarāvat ||
english: May this our sacrifice reach the gods; may the altar reach the upper altar. I release the officiating priests with the sacrificial fees — may the gods worship again as before.

sanskrit: yajña yajñaṃ gaccha yajñapatiṃ gaccha | svāṃ yoniṃ gaccha svāhā ||
english: O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice; go to the lord of the sacrifice. Go to your own womb. Svāhā!

sanskrit: eṣa te yajño yajamāna sahasūktanamovākaḥ | suvīraḥ svāhā ||
english: This is your sacrifice, O sacrificer, accompanied by a thousand sūktas and salutations. Rich in heroes. Svāhā!

sanskrit: manasaspata imaṃ deva yajñam | svāhā vāci svāhā vāte dhāḥ svāhā ||
english: O Lord of the Mind, O god, this sacrifice — place svāhā in speech, place svāhā in the wind. Svāhā!

sanskrit: svāhā hutebhyo vaṣaḍ ḍhutebhyaḥ | devā gātuvido gātuṃ vittvā gātum ita svāhā ||
english: Svāhā to those for whom the oblation is offered; vaṣaṭ to those for whom it is offered with the exclamation. O gods who know the path, having found the path, go the path from here. Svāhā!

sanskrit: saṃ barhir aktaṃ haviṣā ghṛtena sam indreṇa vasubhiḥ saṃ marudbhiḥ | saṃ devebhir viśvadevebhir aktam indraṃ gacchatu yat svāhā ||
english: The barhis anointed together with oblation and ghee, united with Indra, with the Vasus, united with the Maruts — anointed together with the gods and the All-Gods, may whatever is offered with svāhā go to Indra.

sanskrit: āśāsānā saumanasaṃ prajāṃ cakṣur atho balam | indrāṇyā anuvrataṃ saṃ nahye amṛtāya kam ||
english: Hoping for good will, for progeny, for sight, and also for strength — following the vow of Indrāṇī, I bind myself for the sake of immortal bliss.

sanskrit: indrāṇī nārī subhagā supatny ud aṃśena patividye bibheda | triṃśad yasyā jaghanaṃ yojanāny upastha indraṃ sthaviraṃ pipartu ||
english: Indrāṇī, blessed woman and good wife, burst forth with her shoulder to be known to her husband. She whose hips span thirty yojanas — may her lap carry venerable Indra.

sanskrit: senāsi pṛthivī dhanaṃjay- -āditir viśvarūpā sūryatvak | indrāṇī prāṣāṭ saṃjayantī tasyai ta enā haviṣā vidhema ||
english: You are an army, earth-wide, wealth-conquering; Aditi of all forms, with a sun-skin. Indrāṇī who strikes forward, all-conquering — with this oblation we honor her.

sanskrit: ajirottiṣṭhanty utthitāgre tvarī prāṣāṭ tūrtam upacarantīm | prāṣāṭ kas tvariṣā tvāgre tvarikas tvayiṣamesa tvā bhadre ||
english: Rising swiftly, rising at the fore, the swift one strikes forward, hastening rapidly to attend. The swift one strikes forward — who with swiftness? You at the fore; O swift one, may this swiftness here be for you, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: paryāvarte duṣvapnyāt pāpāt svapnād abhūtyāḥ | brahmāham antaraṃ kṛṇve parā svapnamukhāḥ śucaḥ ||
english: I turn away from ill-dreaming, from evil dream, from misfortune. I make the brahman my inner shield — let the sorrows that show their face in dreams depart.

sanskrit: yat svapne annam aśnāmi na prātar adhigamyate | sarvaṃ tad astu naḥ śivaṃ nahi tad dṛśyate divā ||
english: Whatever food I eat in a dream that is not found in the morning — may all that be auspicious for us, for it is not seen by daylight.
